img: In the night the gale tore the old fence down
text: One nail still holds a fencepost, half-buried where the rest went down. The gale of Hagalaz left the field wide open, and what stood as a border is now just wood on wet grass. You can see further now than the fence ever allowed. Kuky, which line were you keeping, and would you build it back?

img: The shavings curl away from the blade
text: The blade stays where the hand holds it, and everything else curls away in thin pale ribbons. That steadiness is where Kenaz sits, the light by which the shape is found. You are cutting away, Kuky, more than you are adding. What has come clear under your hands lately, and what would you do with it now that you have seen it?

img: The sweater you knitted all winter is finally finished
text: The sweater lies finished across your knees, the needles set aside, the basket of yarn nearly empty. In that quiet weight of wool there is Jera, the plain worth of something worked at through a long season. You cannot see the winter in it now, only the thing itself. What you carry may have been shaped long before you knew what shape it would take.

img: You keep knitting though the yarn is almost out
text: The needles keep moving, and the yarn thins toward its end in your hand. Nauthiz sits in that last stretch of thread, where the work goes on past what there is to work with. You are not resting, you are finishing. Kuky, this may be the point where the need itself becomes visible to you.

img: Someone calls your name across the crowd
text: At the edge of the noise, one voice carries your name and the crowd thins to nothing. In that turn from din to a single sound sits Ansuz, the moment hearing becomes listening. Between two people, the words already spoken may be waiting for that same quiet. Perhaps you have not heard them yet, or perhaps you heard and have not answered.

img: One hand holds something out, and the other receives it
text: You stand where one hand holds something out and another comes to meet it, neither yet closed. In that small distance between palms, Gebo lives. What is offered here, Kuky, has not been counted, and what is taken has not been weighed. Between you and someone, this may be generosity and debt at once, given freely and still waiting.
